items.question: What exact embedding dimensionality did LINE use in its experiments on language, social, and citation networks?
items.why_unanswerable: The passage says LINE was evaluated on several real-world networks and tasks, but it never reports the embedding dimensionality used in those experiments.
items.evidence_quote: We evaluate the performance of the LINE with various real-world information networks, including language networks, social networks, and citation networks.

items.question: How many nodes and edges were in the largest graph used to benchmark LINE on real-world information networks?
items.why_unanswerable: The passage claims LINE can scale to millions of nodes and billions of edges, but it does not give the size of any specific benchmark graph.
items.evidence_quote: It is able to learn the embedding of a network with millions of nodes and billions of edges in a few hours on a single machine.

items.question: Under which exact hyperparameter settings did LINE achieve the best word analogy accuracy compared with its baselines?
items.why_unanswerable: The passage mentions word analogy as one of the evaluation tasks and says LINE outperforms baselines, but it provides no hyperparameter values or best-setting analysis.
items.evidence_quote: The effectiveness of the learned embeddings is evaluated within multiple data mining tasks, including word analogy, text classification, and node classification.

items.question: What was the runtime of LINE on a GPU server, and how did that compare numerically with the single-machine runtime reported in the paper?
items.why_unanswerable: The passage only states that LINE can learn embeddings in a few hours on a single machine; it does not report any GPU-server runtime or a numerical comparison against it.
items.evidence_quote: It is able to learn the embedding of a network with millions of nodes and billions of edges in a few hours on a single machine.
